It has a large BigQuery dataset of customer-feedback text containing varied language patterns, emojis, and slang. You want to create a solution that classifies sentiment from this feedback text. What should you do?

options.text: Preprocess the text data in BigQuery using SQL functions. Export the processed data to AutoML Natural Language for model training and deployment.
Develop a custom sentiment analysis model using TensorFlow. Deploy it on a Compute Engine instance.
Use Dataproc to create a Spark cluster, perform text preprocessing using Spark NLP, and build a sentiment analysis model with Spark MLlib.
Export the raw data from BigQuery. Use AutoML Natural Language to train a custom sentiment analysis model.

questions.explanation:
AutoML Natural Language provides managed custom sentiment-model training and deployment from labeled text, avoiding the operational and machine-learning engineering overhead of building and hosting a TensorFlow or Spark MLlib model. Using the raw review text retains sentiment-bearing language, emojis, and slang for the custom text model. AutoML Text is now deprecated, with Google directing new custom text classification and sentiment workloads to Vertex AI Gemini prompting and tuning.

options.text: Configure the buckets to use the Archive storage class.
Configure a lifecycle management policy on each bucket to downgrade the storage class and remove objects based on age.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management applies rules based on conditions such as object age. Its `SetStorageClass` action can move older objects to lower-cost classes, and its `Delete` action can remove objects after the required retention period, aligning cost optimization with defined tiering and retention policies.

**Learn more:** [Object Lifecycle Management | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a BigQuery table used for critical end-of-month reporting. The table receives new sales data every week. You need to avoid data loss and reporting problems if the table is accidentally deleted. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the time travel duration on the table to be exactly seven days. On deletion, re-create the deleted table solely from the time travel data.
Schedule the creation of a new snapshot of the table once a week. On deletion, re-create the deleted table using the snapshot and time travel data.
Create a clone of the table. On deletion, re-create the deleted table by copying the content of the clone.
Create a view of the table. On deletion, re-create the deleted table from the view and time travel data.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery table snapshots retain a point-in-time copy independently of the base table and can be restored to a writable table. They provide retention beyond BigQuery time travel’s maximum seven-day recovery window, while time travel can recover more recent changes made after the latest weekly snapshot when the deletion is within that window.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to table snapshots](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/table-snapshots-intro) · [Restore deleted tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/restore-deleted-tables)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an online retail company. Use Dataflow to implement a streaming pipeline using an OBJECT_FINALIZE notification from Pub/Sub to read the data from Cloud Storage, perform the transformations, and write the data to BigQuery.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization has a BigQuery dataset containing sensitive employee information, including salaries and performance reviews. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Looker analyst who needs to add a new field to a Looker report that generates SQL to run against your company’s database. You do not have the Develop permission. What should you do?

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a data analyst at your organization and have been given a BigQuery dataset containing customer information. Use Cloud Data Fusion to create a data pipeline to read the data from BigQuery, perform data quality transformations, and write the clean data back to BigQuery.

Use BigQuery's built-in functions to perform data quality transformations.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery can clean and transform data in place with GoogleSQL expressions and data-manipulation features. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a data-ingestion pipeline that loads small CSV files from Cloud Storage into BigQuery. Create a Cloud Composer pipeline to load new files from Cloud Storage to BigQuery and schedule it to run every 10 minutes.
Create a Cloud Run function to load the data into BigQuery that is triggered when data arrives in Cloud Storage.
Create a Dataproc cluster to pull CSV files from Cloud Storage, process them using Spark, and write the results to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:

Export the historical data as a CSV file. Import the file into BigQuery for analysis. Use Cloud Composer for daily automation.
Export the historical data to BigQuery by using BigQuery Data Transfer Service. Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service for daily automation.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a data analyst handling sensitive customer data in BigQuery. Encrypt the data by using customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).
Update dataset privileges by using the SQL GRANT statement.
Export the data to Cloud Storage, and use signed URLs to authorize access.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery uses IAM roles to control access to its resources. Granting authorized principals the least-permissive predefined or custom roles at the appropriate resource scope provides the permissions required to query the data without granting unnecessary access.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization must retain historical customer order data. Store the data in Cloud Storage using Coldline storage.
Store the data in Cloud Storage using Standard storage.
Store the data in Cloud Storage using Archive storage.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Nearline is a low-cost class intended for data read or modified on average once per month or less, including data accessed monthly for analysis. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database that holds sensitive historical financial data. You must ensure the data remains uncorrupted and can be recovered if the primary region is destroyed. Because the data is valuable, prioritize the recovery point objective (RPO) over the recovery time objective (RTO). You want to recommend a solution that minimizes latency for primary read and write operations. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance for multi-region backup locations.
Configure the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance for regional availability (HA) with synchronous replication to a secondary instance in a different zone.
Configure the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance for regional availability (HA) with asynchronous replication to a secondary instance in a different region.
Configure the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance for regional availability (HA). Back up the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database hourly to a Cloud Storage bucket in a different region.

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL multi-region backups provide disaster-recovery capability for a regional outage while retaining the primary database in its local region, avoiding synchronous cross-region write latency. Cloud SQL high availability uses synchronous replication only between zones within the configured region, so it does not protect against loss of that entire region. Cross-region replicas replicate asynchronously and can lose recent committed transactions during a regional outage.

**Learn more:** [Manage standard backups | Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/backup-recovery/manage-standard-backups) · [About high availability | Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/high-availability)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is establishing an enterprise business intelligence platform. You must restrict data access across many different teams while following Google’s recommended approach. What should you do first?

Create one Looker Studio report with multiple pages, and add each team's data as a separate data source to the report.
Create a Looker (Google Cloud core) instance, and create a separate dashboard for each team.
Create a Looker (Google Cloud core) instance, and configure different Looker groups for each team.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization must implement near-real-time analytics for thousands of events that arrive each second in Pub/Sub. Create a Cloud Data Fusion instance and configure Pub/Sub as a source. Use Data Fusion to process the Pub/Sub messages, perform transformations, and write the results to BigQuery.

Load the data from Pub/Sub into Cloud Storage using a Cloud Storage subscription. Create a Dataproc cluster, use PySpark to perform transformations in Cloud Storage, and write the results to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has chosen to migrate its existing enterprise data warehouse to BigQuery. Use the Cloud Data Fusion web interface to build data pipelines. Create a directed acyclic graph (DAG) that facilitates pipeline orchestration.
Use the existing data pipeline tool’s BigQuery connector to reconfigure the data mapping.
Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to recreate the data pipeline and migrate the data into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:

options.text: ETL; Dataflow -> BigQuery

questions.explanation:

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization sends IoT event data to a Pub/Sub topic. You need to change the pipeline to handle these activity spikes and continue processing messages. What should you do?

options.text: Retry messages until they are acknowledged.
Implement flow control on the subscribers.
Forward unacknowledged messages to a dead-letter topic.
Seek back to the last acknowledged message.

questions.explanation:
Subscriber flow control applies backpressure by limiting outstanding messages or bytes delivered to each subscriber. Once those limits are reached, the subscriber stops pulling more messages until in-flight messages are acknowledged or negatively acknowledged, preventing overload during transient traffic spikes.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a pipeline to process data files that arrive in Cloud Storage by 3:00 am daily. You need to ensure the final output is produced as quickly as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Design a Spark program that runs under Dataproc. Code the program to wait for user input when an error is detected. Rerun the last action after correcting any stage output data errors.
Design the pipeline as a set of PTransforms in Dataflow. Restart the pipeline after correcting any stage output data errors.
Design the workflow as a Cloud Workflow instance. Code the workflow to jump to a given stage based on an input parameter. Rerun the workflow after correcting any stage output data errors.
Design the processing as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer. Clear the state of the failed task after correcting any stage output data errors.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a web application that stores its data in a Cloud SQL database. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s ecommerce website receives product reviews from customers. You work for a financial services company that processes highly sensitive data. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must retain complete, manual control over data encryption. Which type of keys should you recommend for data storage?

options.text: Use customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK).
Use a dedicated third-party key management system (KMS) chosen by the company.
Use Google-managed encryption keys (GMEK).
Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).

questions.explanation:
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) keep key material under the customer’s control: the customer supplies the key for storage operations, and Google Cloud does not permanently store or otherwise manage that key. This provides the required direct, manual control of encryption keys.

**Learn more:** [Customer-supplied encryption keys | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-supplied-keys) · [Customer-supplied encryption keys | Security | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption/customer-supplied-encryption-keys)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a data pipeline to process sensitive customer data kept in a Cloud Storage bucket. You must ensure the data remains accessible even if a single-zone outage occurs. What should you do?

options.text: Set up a Cloud CDN in front of the bucket.
Enable Object Versioning on the bucket.
Store the data in a multi-region bucket.
Store the data in Nearline storage.

questions.explanation:
A multi-region Cloud Storage bucket provides redundancy across geographically separated regions and remains available during failures, including a single-zone outage. Object Versioning addresses accidental deletion or replacement, Cloud CDN is a content-delivery cache, and Nearline is an access/cost storage class rather than a bucket-location resilience mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage bucket locations](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-locations) · [Cloud Storage data availability and durability](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/availability-durability)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization stores highly sensitive data across multiple BigQuery datasets, and that data is updated once per day. You need to give a new data analyst access to query specific BigQuery data while preventing access to sensitive data. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the data analyst the BigQuery Job User IAM role in the Google Cloud project.
Create a materialized view with the limited data in a new dataset. Grant the data analyst BigQuery Data Viewer IAM role in the dataset and the BigQuery Job User IAM role in the Google Cloud project.
Create a new Google Cloud project, and copy the limited data into a BigQuery table. Grant the data analyst the BigQuery Data Owner IAM role in the new Google Cloud project.
Grant the data analyst the BigQuery Data Viewer IAM role in the Google Cloud project.

questions.explanation:
The BigQuery Job User role grants permission to create query jobs in the project, while BigQuery Data Viewer granted only on a dedicated dataset limits readable data to that dataset. A materialized view that exposes only the permitted data must be configured as an authorized view when the analyst is not granted access to its base tables; this lets the view access source data without granting the analyst direct source-table access.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are moving data from a legacy, on-premises MySQL database to Google Cloud. The database has multiple tables of varying data types and sizes, including large tables containing millions of rows and transactional data. options.text: Set up a Cloud Composer environment to orchestrate a custom data pipeline. Use a Python script to extract data from the MySQL database and load it to MySQL on Compute Engine.
